## Independence and exact basis

Independent reviewer /root/independent_delivery_review authored none of the implementation or its tests. This agent's earlier participation was Delivery assessment only, not plan or Design authorship. The implementation owner is release-implementation-owner. Review made no engineering, activity or work edits.

Read the complete engineering diff and both new files, the applicable existing generation/preflight/verification consumers, current Design/Delivery allocation and release-m1-implementation-r1 proof. Primary full per-kind context establishes M1 in progress/review ready, M2–M4 pending, current approved design-review-r4/delivery-review-r1 and no preexisting implementation finding. Exact normative Design and primary-plan subjects still match approval. Changed baseline implementation subjects are assessed as the new diff, not presented as unchanged upstream observations. The working implementation matched f2e8a79a during this review.

## Finding release-m1-f1

- Finding ID: release-m1-f1.
- Severity: major.
- Location: scripts/release_candidate.py:27 and :323–372; retained scripts/release-verify.sh and scripts/validate-release.py composition.
- Evidence: prepare_candidate creates its own CANDIDATE_CHECKS success vocabulary and executes profile/preflight, skill and adapter regressions, archive validation, npm regression/package checks and packed installation before sealing. It never invokes the retained full release-verification entrypoint or the required release metadata/evidence validator, and those checks are absent from its mandatory accepted set. release-verify.sh remains unchanged, still rejects the current v0.5.1 target and regenerates archives; validate-release retains release/profile/evidence/security and timing composition that the new path bypasses. The registered integration evidence accurately lists the subset it ran, but that subset does not establish the M1 promise of a verified retained candidate using the same complete command composition. In particular, generated required release/security/evidence fields remain pending while the candidate can be sealed with all its locally defined checks passing.
- Required outcome: complete the allocated M1 full-check boundary. Reuse/adapt the repository-owned full release composition for the sealed C/overlay/artifact basis, including actual required release/evidence/security checks and explicit new-path timing consequence. Missing/failed required correctness facts must prevent a verified/sealed approval-ready candidate; absent/malformed duration telemetry must remain separately diagnostic as approved. Do not substitute a third hand-maintained definition of complete release correctness.
- Safe resolution path: implement the already-approved M1 validator/composition integration and necessary supported-profile consumers, preserving legacy/special applicability. Add direct negative proof that an otherwise valid package with failed/missing required release facts cannot complete candidate preparation, and execute the real successful candidate path through the complete applicable command set. If the author instead proposes moving allocated M1 work, return to plan and independent Delivery reassessment before claiming M1 complete; silently leaving this for M3 is not a disposition.
- needs-decision rationale: none for completing the approved allocation.

REL-SR-08/09 and M1's scope, completion criteria and TG-02 require real full checks and preserved required validation before the candidate is considered verified. M3 owns hosted integration and the complete operator path; it does not retroactively supply a missing M1 correctness boundary. Passing existing lower-level suites is useful evidence but cannot prove an unexecuted gate. The candidate's positive test compares its recorded set to the same CANDIDATE_CHECKS constant, so it cannot expose this missing-owner-check defect.

## Finding release-m1-f2

- Finding ID: release-m1-f2.
- Severity: major.
- Location: scripts/release_transaction.py:343–361, particularly the whole-document replacement at line 354.
- Evidence: approval_driven preparation converts every '| pass |' and ': pass\n' occurrence in each planned Markdown/YAML file, including human-authored text outside generated regions. Existing release-note generation first preserves surrounding narrative; this new postprocessing then rewrites it. The special preservation branch protects only the standing record, not release notes or other human-preserving surfaces. A reviewer-run isolated reproduction using the existing PrepareReleaseTests.make_repo fixture and a release-note human section containing '| Existing result | pass |' changed that exact row to '| Existing result | pending |'. No generated marker owned that human row.
- Required outcome: generate pending expectations only in fields/regions actually owned by preparation. Preserve all human narrative outside generated regions byte-for-byte and preserve finalized/historical records already selected for retention by the existing helpers. No blanket textual replacement may reinterpret an existing human or observed result as pending.
- Safe resolution path: change the owning generated-value construction or narrowly scoped generated-region transformation; add a failing-before/passing-after regression for human pass-like text outside a release-note region and retain standing-record/idempotency protection. Include protected finalized results where the generation helpers intentionally return existing bytes. Rerun the affected preparation/candidate proof and independent M1 review.
- needs-decision rationale: none; REL-SR-04/05 and the M1 preservation boundary already require the result.

The reproduction ran only in a temporary repository fixture and did not alter reviewed files. It created docs/releases/v0.3.5/release-notes.md with a human compatibility table and invoked prepare_release('v0.3.5', root=fixture, approval_driven=True). Observed preservation before=True, after=False; observed resulting row='| Existing result | pending |'. This is an actual data-preservation failure, not a hypothetical string-style concern.

## First-pass checklist

| Criterion | Result | Evidence |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Spec alignment | concern | Full-check ownership/composition and human-content preservation violate allocated M1 obligations above. |
| Test coverage | concern | Actual full archive/package/packed-init path is valuable; tests do not detect omitted owner gates or human text rewritten outside the standing record. |
| Edge cases | concern | Version/profile/check unknowns, source/evidence-ref collision, symlink/path escape and post-seal tampering have direct tests; the preserved-content counterexample fails and full release-fact rejection remains unproved. |
| Error handling | concern | Subprocess failure/zero-test handling and candidate mismatch rejection are explicit, but an omitted required validator cannot surface its failure. |
| Architecture boundaries | concern | The ordered C/archive/metadata/index/pack/outer evidence chain is present; a second local complete-check list diverges from the retained release owner. |
| Compatibility | concern | Default preparation remains opt-in unchanged, yet the selected new mode can rewrite preserved narrative and potentially retained observed fields. |
| Security/privacy | concern | Fixed command arrays and suppressed subprocess environment/stderr reduce exposure; missing required release/security composition prevents a clean overall safety conclusion. No actual publisher was added. |
| Derived artifact currency | pass within tested scope | Registered real integration observes three archive identities, packed bundled metadata/index, exact C and all three packed init paths; post-check artifact mutation rejects. This is fixture evidence, not public release correctness. |
| Unrelated changes | pass | Four code/test files plus attributable change records; no public package version, remote configuration, source retirement or M2/M3 publisher change. |
| Validation evidence | concern | The 119 release tests and seven npm tests are recorded on exact subjects, but their passed subset does not satisfy the omitted full gate. Independent reproduction contradicts the broader preservation claim. |

## Supported partial results and limits

The implementation provides a useful candidate foundation: exact source ref/commit checks, deterministic prepared-commit attribution, bounded generated paths, separate metadata overlay, immutable artifact manifest, raw-byte verification, actual bundled metadata-before-pack ordering, packed CLI init for all targets and no publication call. Existing default helpers and historical timing validation remain untouched unless approval_driven is selected. Missing timing is returned as a diagnostic by the new wrapper after profile validation. These supported facts do not erase the required corrections or close M1.

M2 execution/approval persistence, M3 hosted setup and one-approval workflow, and M4 source deletion are intentionally absent under the approved sequence; they are not findings against this slice. New real publication/configuration is not requested or authorized by this review.

Actually performed: complete diff/new-file inspection; scoped existing consumer reads; required code-review guidance and result/finding assets; full primary context/evidence/subject inspection; normative identity comparison; the isolated preparation-preservation reproduction described above; finding/review command help; targeted recording and scoped record validation/diff whitespace checks. The reviewer inspected the registered 119/7-test results but did not rerun those expensive suites. No hosted CI, remote write, publication or customer installation was performed. Original tests/evidence remain as recorded; successful checks are not relabeled failed, and their broader unsupported interpretation is identified explicitly.
